summary: Geo-cache affinity / sticky-routing mis-evaluation causing cross-region tail latency and stream timeouts for customer requests
description: Issue summary: Finora Analytics reported repeated inference request timeouts and elevated tail latency (p95-p99) for streaming responses from their production workload in us-west. Impact: affects customer-facing feature that streams partial outputs to end users; multiple sessions experienced open-stream cancellations and 504s. Initial triage noted cross-region hops to eu-west for requests originating in us-west.
impact: End users experienced delayed or aborted streaming completions; customer reports increased error rate from ~0.2% baseline to ~9% during the incident window. Business impact: degraded UX for critical dashboarding feature during peak trading hours for Finora.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send streaming generate requests from a client in us-west against the hosted API for model open-gpt-13b-v2 at ~120 RPS with 1-2s average prefix length.
2) Observe X-Redwood-Route and X-Response-Region headers on responses (some requests return eu-west).
3) Reproduce with customer headers (x-redwood-customer-id: finora-01); note elevated handshake times and occasional 'stream closed by server' events.
4) Run agent: curl -v to /v1/stream with --header 'x-redwood-region: us-west' to validate mitigation.
5) Use internal routing debug endpoint /internal/routing/debug?request_id=<id> to see affinity key evaluation and fallback decisions.
logs: Error sample: 'KVCache miss, falling back to remote shard. consistent_hash_seed mismatch during rebalance.'
Route telemetry shows a spike in 'affinity_evaluation_errors' at 2026-03-10T09:12-09:20 UTC coincident with config rollout event id cfg-2026-03-10-02
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: transient network egress or peering causing cross-region hop.
Observed pattern: not every request crossed; correlated with affinity key lookups against local geo-cache returning stale/empty entries which then triggered fallback to compatible region (eu-west).

Found root cause: a config change (cfg-2026-03-10-02) shortened geo-cache affinity TTL and changed consistent-hash seed rotation to 'fast-reconcile' mode. During the reconcile window shards returned inconsistent hash results, producing affinity_mismatch errors and fallback routing to eu-west.

Supporting evidence: routing debug traces show different consistent_hash_seed values between edge-proxy and smart-router for the same timestamp. Telemetry: 'affinity_mismatch' metric increased 4300% during rollout window. No network packet drops observed on egress, ruling out peering blackholes.

Customer-specific behaviour: Finora's workload creates many short-lived session keys (per-user ephemeral IDs). With shortened TTL, cache churn increased, amplifying the mismatch frequency for this customer.
Temporary mitigation validated: pinning region via 'x-redwood-region: us-west' header keeps traffic local and prevents fallback; rolling back cfg-2026-03-10-02 removed the mismatch entirely.
Contributors: routing (Liam C.), edge-proxy (Aria S.), cache team (Owen M.), SRE (Ravi K.).
comments: Maya Patel (Support): Customer reported first errors at 09:12 UTC. Opening ticket and escalated to SRE. Added customer-impact tag.
Liam Chen (Routing): Initial probe shows affinity_mismatch spike. Pulling recent config deployments and will correlate with rollout timeline.
Aria Suzuki (Edge): We saw inconsistent hash seeds between versions during a fast-reconcile; repeating a rollback to previous stable seed resolves path selection.
Finora (Customer): We started seeing streaming disconnects and '504 Upstream timeout' in our user logs around 09:14 UTC. Applying header pin prevented further errors; please advise permanent fix.
Ravi K (SRE): Rolled back cfg-2026-03-10-02 at 09:28 UTC; metrics returned to baseline by 09:40 UTC. Continuing to monitor.
Maya Patel (Support): Sent workaround and apology to customer; scheduled postmortem with teams.
root_cause: Configuration rollout changed geo-cache affinity TTL and enabled fast consistent-hash seed rotation which, during shard reconciliation, produced inconsistent hash results across edge-proxy and routing components. This caused cache affinity mismatches and fallback cross-region routing to eu-west, producing higher latencies and stream timeouts.
resolution: Rolled back cfg-2026-03-10-02 to previous stable config at 2026-03-10T09:28:00Z. Deployed hotfix to add gating check to consistent-hash seed rotation and increased default affinity TTL. Monitored for 2 hours; customer error rate returned to baseline. Issued customer communication and provided header-based region pinning as short-term mitigation.
workaround: Customers can set 'x-redwood-region: us-west' to enforce local routing until a full fix is deployed. Dedicated capacity customers can use their dedicated endpoints which bypass geo-fallback behavior.
follow_up_actions: 1) Create rollout gating: require identical consistent_hash_seed across edge-proxy and router before enabling rotation (PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/smart-router/pull/884).
2) Increase default geo-cache affinity TTL for ephemeral-session workloads and add metric to detect TTL-induced churn.
3) Add alert: affinity_mismatch_rate > 50/min triggers automated rollback of the seed-rotation feature flag.
4) Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC; owners: Liam Chen, Aria Suzuki, Owen Mitchell.
5) Customer follow-up: Provide formal RCA and compensation request channel; CS lead to own communications.
resolution_notes: Hotfix and rollback completed; monitoring shows stable routing and normal streaming success rates. Customer accepted workaround and will review RCA. Action items scheduled in engineering backlog.
resolution_status: Mitigated (hotfix & rollback); RCA in progress; customer notified
